editorial:
Imagine having all the money in the world but feeling like your life is totally empty. That is exactly where you find Tim, a rich kid in Los Angeles who has everything on paper but nothing in his heart. After his parents split up, he goes on a wild ride of partying and drug use just to numb the pain. It is a heavy setup, but it feels real because you see a teenager who is just lost and looking for someone to actually care about him. The vibe is a mix of glamorous L.A. parties and the cold, hard reality of a mental hospital.

You will probably be impressed by the acting, as the emotions feel raw and honest. While the story moves a bit slow in the middle, the bond between Tim and his doctor provides a nice spark of hope. If you like stories about overcoming hard times, you should definitely give this a try. You can find it by renting it on Apple TV or adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best quality. It is a great pick for a quiet night when you want something that makes you think about life.
endingExplained: In the end, Tim finally stops fighting everyone and starts listening to his doctor. He realizes that his parents' divorce isn't his fault and that he can't find happiness in pills or parties. He manages to break his cycle of self-destruction and decides to take responsibility for his own life. The movie wraps up with Tim feeling a sense of peace and hope, showing that he is finally ready to grow up and heal.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt stories about mental health and family struggle.
